hypotheses.title: Options Put-Call Ratio Regime Switch with Volatility Skew and Intraday Gain Dispersion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Exploits options open-interest sentiment regime shifts via trade_when(pcr_oi_270 > ts_mean(pcr_oi_10, 190)). When the 270-day put-call ratio exceeds its trailing 190-day mean of the 10-day PCR, the market regime triggers an asymmetric implied volatility skew position (implied_volatility_call_360 - implied_volatility_put_1080) with currency neutralization. Modulating with backfilled standard deviation of intraday 4-percent gain arrival times (minutes_to_four_percent_gain_2) scales capital into instruments with high microstructure momentum dispersion.
confounders: Sudden currency devaluations impacting multi-currency options surfaces
Protracted periods of extreme market-wide implied volatility compression
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if intraday gain dispersion does not scale with post-regime options volatility expansion.
